description: Which message a failed verification shows and the one action it offers. A failure is either refused when the job is submitted, which the SDK reports with the HTTP status, or returned after the job was accepted, with a `reason`. Each app's resolver holds this table and a unit test asserts it row for row and case for case. `message` and `button` are keys in `l10n/app/`. The messages say what the user can do and never why a verification was refused, and no server text is ever shown.
matching: Rows are tried in order and the first match wins. A submission row matches on `status` or `transport`, a result row on `reasons`. A row with `serverMessageContains` also needs the server's message to contain one of its entries, ignoring case, so it sits above the plain row for the same status or reason. Nothing matching resolves as the `fallback` row.

retry.does: Runs the verification again as a new job. The button stays visible and is dimmed for the row's `backoffSeconds`, one entry per use, and for `waitsFor` while that holds.

retryLater.does: As `retry`, with a longer delay and a single use.

recapture.does: Restarts capture, then submits a new job.

fixInput.does: Returns to the ID form. No new capture.

newSession.does: Takes a new token and restarts the flow.

exit.does: Ends the flow. No retry is offered, and the error still reaches the host app.

limits: `maxUses` on a row overrides its action's. `per: session` counts every use of the action in the session, `per: error` counts uses for one error. A row with neither has no limit. A use past the last `backoffSeconds` entry waits the last entry again, so a row with one entry waits that long before every use. When a limit is reached the button is replaced by Close.

fallback.why: A status or reason the table does not name gets a message that names nothing and a Close button: a retry that fails the same way is not offered, and an unknown refusal is never explained.

unsubmitted.why: A run that failed before any submission has no row: the user declined consent or the camera, or the flow could not be built. Nothing reached the server, so the message says only that and blames no one, and the result card keeps the SDK's own error in debug builds.

notDistinguished.why: The API documents no response text for it, so an app cannot tell it from the other 403 answers. Both end in Close.

notDistinguished.cause: Token rejected after the flow began
notDistinguished.why: The API documents no response text for it either. Until it does, the app offers Close where a new session would help.
